info.name: BloodLink API
info.description:
Every endpoint in the BloodLink backend (Spring Boot 4 / Java 25), organised by module exactly as the codebase is: auth, donor (self), donor lookup, blood banks, hospitals, inventory, blood requests, appeals, notifications, admin (users + reports), and donations.

**Auth model.** Every route except `/api/health`, `/api/auth/register` and `/api/auth/login` requires a bearer token. The **Register** and **Login** requests in the Auth folder each carry a small test script that reads the response and saves the token into a collection variable named after the account's role — `donorToken`, `hospitalStaffToken`, `bankStaffToken` or `adminToken` — plus `<role>UserId`, `<role>BloodBankId` / `<role>HospitalId` where relevant. Every other request in this collection authenticates with `{{donorToken}}`, `{{bankStaffToken}}`, etc., so running Register/Login once per role wires up the rest of the collection automatically.

**Roles CLAUDE.md's schema does not let you self-register.** Only DONOR accounts can be created via `POST /api/auth/register`. HOSPITAL_STAFF, BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN accounts have no creation endpoint at all — in this project they only ever exist by a direct database insert (an administrator's own account-management tooling, or a developer seeding one by hand). To exercise the Blood Bank / Hospital / Admin folders, first register a donor, then promote that same account by hand, e.g.:

```sql
delete from donors where user_id = '<the user id>';
update users set role = 'BLOOD_BANK_STAFF', blood_bank_id = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111' where id = '<the user id>';
```

(`11111111-…` is Makeni Regional Blood Bank's fixed seed id — see `V4__seed_blood_banks.sql`; `33333333-…` is Makeni Regional Hospital's, from `V6__seed_hospitals.sql`. Both blood bank ids and both hospital ids are collection variables below, pre-filled with these seeded values.) Then re-run **Login** for that phone number to capture a fresh, role-correct token.

**Blood group values in URLs.** Wherever a blood group is a path or query parameter (never in a JSON body, which needs no special handling), the literal `+` must be percent-encoded as `%2B` — a raw `+` in a URL decodes as a space server-side. Every request below that needs this already has it built in.

**Error shape.** Every failure — 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, or an unexpected 500 — returns the same JSON shape: `{ timestamp, status, error, message, fieldErrors? }`. `fieldErrors` is present only for a validation failure (a bad request body field, or a constrained query parameter), mapping the failing field name to a message safe to show directly to a user.

**Real-time channel.** `/ws` (STOMP over SockJS) pushes the four Notification types live to a connected client. It is not a request/response endpoint and is not represented in this collection — see `WebSocketConfig` and `StompAuthChannelInterceptor` in the source. `GET /api/notifications` and `GET /api/notifications/unread-count` are this collection's way of reading what that channel would otherwise push.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Public endpoints — no token required, and none accepted. Registration only ever creates a DONOR (CLAUDE.md: staff and admin accounts are never self-registered).

request.description: `bloodType` may be `null` for "I don't know yet" (Business Rule 4 — it is re-verified at every donation regardless). `gender` is one of `MALE`, `FEMALE`, `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`. On success (201), the token and user id are saved to `donorToken` / `donorUserId` automatically.

exec: const roleKey = { DONOR: 'donor', HOSPITAL_STAFF: 'hospitalStaff', BLOOD_BANK_STAFF: 'bankStaff', ADMIN: 'admin' }[body.user.role];
pm.test('captured token for role ' + body.user.role, () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Re-run this with `hospitalStaffPhone`/`hospitalStaffPassword`, `bankStaffPhone`/`bankStaffPassword` or `adminPhone`/`adminPassword` in the body (edit the raw JSON, or duplicate this request) once those accounts exist, to capture a token for each role. The response shape is identical to Register's.

item.name: Donor (Self)
item.description: Every route here is scoped to the caller by their own token — there is no id parameter, and no way to look up a different donor's profile from this folder. Requires DONOR (or ADMIN, though an admin has no donor profile to see).

request.description: Dashboard summary: blood type, eligibility (Business Rule 2), totals, lives impacted, first/last donation dates.
Full history, most recent first. `bloodType` on each row is the group tested at that donation (Business Rule 4) — it can differ from, or exist where, the profile's own blood type does not.

item.name: Donor Lookup (Blood Bank)
item.description: The one place a donor's details are shown to someone else — restricted to BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN, the opposite of the Donor (Self) folder's rule. Feeds the Record Donation flow.

request.description: Exact phone match only — no browse, no partial-name search. 404 (with a message telling you what to do next) if nobody matches. On success, saves `donorId` to `donorLookupId` for the Donations folder.

item.name: Blood Banks
item.description: Fixed, seeded reference data (CLAUDE.md — two banks, never self-registering). The plain listing is open to any signed-in role; the dashboard is staff-facing.

request.description: Any signed-in role. The two seeded banks, for pickers and read-only display.
BLOOD_BANK_STAFF or ADMIN only. The four Blood Bank Dashboard stat cards: total units, donations this month, pending requests, registered donors.

item.name: Hospitals
item.description: Fixed, seeded reference data (CLAUDE.md — two hospitals, never self-registering). No write path exists at all.

request.description: Any signed-in role.

item.name: Inventory
item.description: Per-bank, per-blood-group stock — one row per (blood_bank_id, blood_type), not per unit. Reading is open to any signed-in role; writing is BLOOD_BANK_STAFF (own bank only) or ADMIN (any bank).

request.description: Always all eight blood groups, even ones this bank has never stocked (those come back as zero units, status CRITICAL).

Total units, units expiring within 4 weeks, count of groups at CRITICAL, units issued this month, and a Sufficient/Low/Critical composition breakdown — backs the Blood Inventory detail page's stat cards and charts.

url.description: The blood-type path segment is percent-encoded — `O%2B` is "O+". Swap for any of A%2B, A-, B%2B, B-, AB%2B, AB-, O-.

request.description: Adds units to the (bank, group) row, creating it if the bank has never stocked that group. Business Rule 7: units accumulate, and the row's expiry becomes the *earlier* of its current expiry and this one — never extended. `unitsToAdd` must be 1–1000 (a typo guard, not a clinical limit); `expiryDate` must not be in the past. BLOOD_BANK_STAFF may only write to their own bank; the check is server-side regardless of which id is in the URL.

item.name: Blood Requests
item.description: The hospital-to-blood-bank sequence (Figure 3.5, Business Rules 5 & 6). HOSPITAL_STAFF submit and track; BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN approve, reject or fulfil.

request.description: HOSPITAL_STAFF only. No hospital id in the body — the caller's own hospital is stamped on server-side. `urgencyLevel` is one of `ROUTINE`, `URGENT`, `EMERGENCY`. `unitsRequested` is 1–500 (typo guard). `patientReference` is optional free text, max 255 characters. Starts `PENDING` with no fulfilling bank. Saves the new id to `bloodRequestId`.

HOSPITAL_STAFF see only their own hospital's requests. BLOOD_BANK_STAFF see every unclaimed request plus any their own bank has already claimed (Business Rule 6) — switch the Authorization header to `{{bankStaffToken}}` to see that view instead. ADMIN see everything, or one bank's actionable scope via `?bloodBankId=`.

item.name: List Requests (as Admin, for one bank)

request.description: `bloodBankId` is a view filter, meaningful only for ADMIN or bank staff not yet assigned a bank — it never widens what an assigned staff member can see.

PENDING -> APPROVED (Business Rule 5). Claims the request for the acting bank and takes it out of every other bank's queue. Requires enough stock right now, though nothing is deducted until Fulfil. `bloodBankId` is ignored for BLOOD_BANK_STAFF (their own bank always wins) and required only for ADMIN.
APPROVED -> FULFILLED. The only action that actually deducts stock — re-checked against current inventory, not trusted from Approve. Only the bank that approved may fulfil.

Declines the request on behalf of the acting blood bank — per Business Rule 11 this is per-bank, not shared. It writes a `blood_request_declines` row and removes the request from THIS bank's queue only; the request stays PENDING and fully actionable for every other bank. It becomes REJECTED (and the hospital is notified) only once every blood bank has declined it. Declining twice as the same bank returns 409. Run against a request that is still PENDING (this example reuses `{{bloodRequestId}}`, which the Approve/Fulfil requests above will already have moved past PENDING — submit a fresh request first if you want to see this succeed).

item.name: Appeals
item.description: A blood bank asking donors of one group to come in (Business Rule 1: Blood Bank -> Donor only, never Hospital -> Donor). Restricted to BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN.

request.description: Sends nothing — reports how many eligible donors an appeal for this group would reach right now, and how many are excluded because they are inside Business Rule 2's 90-day recovery window. Backs the confirmation step before actually sending.

Notifies every *eligible* donor of this group — never a donor still inside their recovery window, regardless of how the appeal was sent. `note` is optional free text, max 280 characters. The response reports how many were notified and how many were skipped as ineligible.

**Rate-limited per (bank, blood group) — Business Rule 12.** Two things return 409 here rather than sending anything:

- **No shortage:** the acting bank holds 30 units or more of this group. Note this is *not* the Business Rule 3 badge threshold — a group at 30–39 units still shows a "Low" badge on the Inventory screen and still cannot be appealed for.
- **Cooldown still running:** this bank already appealed for this group recently. The window is 5 hours if stock was under 15 units at that send (CRITICAL tier) or 24 hours if it was 15–29 (LOW tier), and it ends early the moment stock climbs back over the threshold that triggered it (15 or 30 respectively).

A successful send writes or overwrites the bank's `appeal_cooldowns` row for this group, which is what the Inventory screen reads to decide whether its Send Appeal button is live or shows "Appeal Sent.". To see a 409 for yourself, send this twice in a row against a group the bank is short of.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: The REST side of the bell icon — what fills it on page load and how it is cleared. The live WebSocket push (`/ws`) is the other half; see the collection description.

request.description: Any signed-in role — all four receive some notification type. Up to the 50 most recent, newest first. Copy an `id` from the response into the `notificationId` collection variable to try "Mark One Read" below.
Just the bell's badge number.
Clears every unread notification for the caller. Returns the resulting count (zero).
Set `notificationId` first (see "List My Notifications"). A notification belonging to someone else is a 404, not a 403 — the caller has no business learning it exists.

Every account across all four roles, with its linked blood_bank_id/hospital_id where applicable. Copy an `id` other than `{{adminUserId}}` into the `otherUserId` variable to try the suspend/activate request below — an administrator cannot suspend their own account (409).
Takes effect immediately — the account's existing token is rejected on its very next request (JwtAuthenticationFilter checks status on every one), not only at its next login attempt.
Reverses a suspension. `status` is `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED` — the only two values `AccountStatus` allows.
Six months of citywide donation counts, oldest first, current month included. Every month appears even at zero — a quiet month is real data, not a gap.
Citywide counts by outcome — pending, approved, fulfilled, rejected — plus their total, for the donut chart.

item.name: Donations
item.description: Recording a donation — the moment blood actually enters the system: a Donation row, the donor's last-donation date, and the bank's stock, all in one action. Restricted to BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN.

request.description: Run "Look Up Donor by Phone" first to populate `donorId` from `donorLookupId`. `bloodType` is the group **as tested today** — Business Rule 4 means this is never defaulted from the donor's stored profile, by design; you must state it explicitly even if it matches. `unitsDonated` is 1–10 (a typo guard). Refused with 409, and nothing written, if the donor is still inside their 90-day recovery window (Business Rule 2, enforced server-side regardless of what any UI shows). The donation date is always today, set by the server.
